no good, nothing is of any use now!" But have patience,
friend! If we warn people thus, how often are we told: "Yes,
it is all very fine for you to talk! You are not so badly placed
as I!" I think now of the many among us who have lost their
jobs and their money. Who could fail to think of them with
compassion and not understand their natural impatience?
And yet for them too the answer is: patience! Not as a
friendly human warning, for then they might justifiably
retort: "It is easy for you to talk!" But it is the warning of
God's word itself: you must try to bear patiently the load
placed on your shoulders.
Impatience only makes things worse and leads you to em-
bittered and foolish thoughts. Impatience is harmful too for
the community. How much anger and abuse of others
arise from our impatience! On all sides we hear the com-
plaint: "Nothing has become any better than it was form-
erly! In fact we were better off then than now! then there
was more to eat and drink, more tobacco to smoke!" What
blindness of impatient folly! As though things could anyhow
be other than they are! As though we had not to bear the
necessary consequences of our madness and delusions, and
bear them bravely so that we might go forward again! In
queues, in the bustle of business life and in offices, in the
tramshow often is there a lack of patience and courtesy,
and in consequence what mutual recriminations, in a spirit
of bitterness and hatred! And how many people show an
ungrateful and loveless insensibility to the far greater
burdens and misery of others! Moreover how much better
off are we than those unfortunate ones who, driven from
their homes, are seeking refuge with us from East Germany!
No doubt we are involved in difficulties in attempting to
provide them with shelter, but only patience will enable us
to deal effectively with the situation.

impatience leads people astray into downright wrongdoing,
